context:
Goal: CI runs only what can find a new defect.
Problem (rule): the nightly run in claude-settings has found nothing the push runs had not already found, yet your R61 pick keeps it running whenever main is red.
Based on (measured): 45 nightly runs since 2026-09-30: 22 passed, 15 were cancelled, 8 failed, and each of the 8 failures was on a commit whose push run had already failed (read 22:11 CST from GitHub's run list).
Based on (ruling): R61, your pick b at 15:29 CST Nov 12: skip the nightly when main's newest commit is already green.
Departs from: main runs a nightly at 03:17 UTC — option a removes it.
Why yours: it changes a schedule you set today.

options.gain: No run that found nothing in 45 nights, and free runner slots.
options.how: Remove the nightly schedule in claude-settings and from the CI-upkeep skill's advice; a run can still be started by hand.
options.label: Drop the nightly, keep a manual run (recommended)
options.lose: A break from an outside change, such as a runner image or a dependency, shows only at the next push.

options.label: Keep R61 as is: skip when green
options.lose: It still runs on a red main, where it adds nothing.

options.gain: Saves paid minutes, since only private repos pay for runner minutes.
options.how: Private repos drop the nightly; public repos keep it under R61.
options.label: Off in private repos, kept in public ones
options.lose: Two rules for one thing, and the public nightly still found nothing. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

ref: owner chat with the retrospective 22:11 CST Nov 12; retrospective 22:11 CST
title: Should the nightly CI run be dropped?
why: It changes a CI schedule your R61 pick set.
